lines.trans: Are you having a private party here?
Actually we wanted to sit quietly with the girls.
Alright, I will go then, I will not bother you.
What a fine fellow, he just got up and left!
He always knows how to disappear so suddenly.
Forgive me for reminding you of that again.
Work is over, and you are still here?
Are you making extra revenue for our bar today?
We wanted to sit in female company.
Katya, come on, Nikita is our boss!
Let him sit with us for a little while.

words.gloss: to sit for a while; to stay (with someone)

examples.text: Делаете сегодня дополнительную выручку нашему бару?
examples.trans: Are you making extra revenue for our bar today?

examples.text: Ты хотел вчера специально напоить Никиту в баре?
examples.trans: Did you try to get Nikita drunk on purpose yesterday at the bar?

examples.text: Наш бар закрывается.
examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Тем более я гениальный шеф-повар.
examples.trans: Especially since I am a brilliant head chef.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('woman's, female, feminine').

examples.text: Мы хотели посидеть в женской компании.
examples.trans: We wanted to sit in female company.

examples.text: Это всё-таки моя женская честь!
examples.trans: This is my womanly honour, after all!

examples.text: Она купила женский журнал.
examples.trans: She bought a women's magazine.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'companies' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы хотели посидеть в женской компании.
examples.trans: We wanted to sit in female company.

examples.text: А это компания брата Осипенко!
examples.trans: And that is Osipenko's cousin's company!

examples.text: Он работает в крупной компании.
examples.trans: He works at a large company.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кате точно нужно надёжное мужское плечо.
examples.trans: Katya definitely needs a reliable man's shoulder.

examples.text: Ну хорошо, давай попробуем это сделать.
examples.trans: Well alright, let us try to do that.

examples.text: Ну да, это действительно мои усы.
examples.trans: Well yes, this really is my mustache.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лёва, какую ерунду ты сейчас говоришь?
examples.trans: Lyova, what nonsense are you talking right now?

examples.text: Ты обязательно пройдёшь полное обследование.
examples.trans: You will definitely undergo a full medical checkup.

examples.text: Ты уже закончил работу, Лёва?
examples.trans: Have you finished work already, Lyova?

meanings.note: Borrowed from English 'boss' (from Dutch 'baas', master).

examples.text: Катя, ну ты чего, Никита наш босс!
examples.trans: Katya, come on, Nikita is our boss!

examples.text: Будет сделано, мой босс.
examples.trans: It will be done, my boss.

examples.text: Назло тебе и твоему боссу.
examples.trans: Just to spite you and your boss.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let (them)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пусть они лучше сами во всём разбираются.
examples.trans: Let them figure everything out by themselves.

examples.text: Да, пусть решают всё сами.
examples.trans: Yes, let them decide everything themselves.

examples.text: Пусть он немного посидит вместе с нами.
examples.trans: Let him sit with us for a little while.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Просто Лёва немного робкий и хороший.
examples.trans: Lyova is simply a bit shy and kind.

examples.text: Пусть он немного посидит вместе с нами.
examples.trans: Let him sit with us for a little while.

examples.text: Я дома спокойно немного отлежалась.
examples.trans: I lay down quietly at home for a bit.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пусть он немного посидит вместе с нами.
examples.trans: Let him sit with us for a little while.

examples.text: Мы всегда будем вместе, любимый.
examples.trans: We will always be together, my love.

examples.text: Спасибо большое, заходи ужинать вместе с нами!
examples.trans: Thank you very much, come in and have dinner with us!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, Лёва, что там случилось?
examples.trans: Yes, Lyova, what happened over there?

examples.text: Да, это время нам отлично подходит.
examples.trans: Yes, that time suits us very well.

examples.text: Вообще непонятно, чего от него ждать.
examples.trans: There is no telling what to expect from him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, Лёва, что там случилось?
examples.trans: Yes, Lyova, what happened over there?

examples.text: У меня там было важное дело.
examples.trans: I had some important business over there.

examples.text: Да, Анечка, что там с анализами?
examples.trans: Yes, Anechka, what is up with the test results?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'test, analysis' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да, Анечка, что там с анализами?
examples.trans: Yes, Anechka, what is up with the test results?

examples.text: Неужели в анализах что-то не так?
examples.trans: Could something really be wrong in the tests?

examples.text: Я действительно ездил сдавать анализы вместо шефа.
examples.trans: I really did go take the medical tests in the chef's place.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'ужели').

examples.text: Неужели в анализах что-то не так?
examples.trans: Could something really be wrong in the tests?

examples.text: Неужели так трудно найти хороший сюжет?
examples.trans: Is it really so difficult to find a good story?

examples.text: Неужели президент накажет вас за правду?
examples.trans: Will the president really punish you for the truth?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Неужели в анализах что-то не так?
examples.trans: Could something really be wrong in the tests?

examples.text: Может, тогда выпьешь что-нибудь полегче?
examples.trans: Maybe then you will drink something lighter?

examples.text: Если и дарить что-то, то не поцелуй.
examples.trans: If I am going to give something, it will be more than a kiss.
